evidence: From the committed degree-20 generators, independent BFS rebuilds a group of order 3420 with element-order distribution 1:1, 2:171, 3:380, 5:684, 9:1140, 10:684, 19:360.
Independent exhaustive scan of 171*380 order-(2,3) pairs gives exactly 6840 with product order 19; each involution occurs 40 times, each order-3 element 18 times, and each order-19 product 19 times.
The z-class of a witness has size 180 and is disjoint from the class of z^{-1}; the 6840 pairs split into two simultaneous-conjugacy classes of 3420.
Independent Hurwitz BFS verifies pure-braid orbits 3420+3420 and, on all six order patterns, two full-braid orbits of 20520, each meeting every pattern in 3420 triples.

The generation claim follows both from the recorded BSGS witness and the maximal-subgroup argument: a subgroup containing a 19-element lies in a proper maximal containing 19 only if it lies in the odd-order Borel 19:9; such a subgroup cannot also contain the involution x.

ATLAS records the group order, outer automorphism order, degree-20 representation, and existence of standard generators of orders (2,3,19), but not the generation-filtered Nielsen count or braid orbit decomposition.
Targeted searches did not locate the exact 6840 count, two inner classes, or braid decompositions for PSL(2,19). The priority claim is restricted to this exact census.

The inner Nielsen-class count and braid-orbit decomposition are standard reusable invariants in triangle-group/Hurwitz-space computations, and the result supplies exact witnesses and a complete finite census for the ATLAS standard-generator type.

reproducibility: The group, exact-order pair count, class split, and both pure and full Hurwitz orbit decompositions were independently recomputed directly from the committed S,T permutations.

limitations: The phrase 'reduced Hurwitz covering degree' is potentially nonstandard for this three-branch-point situation; the rigorously verified invariant is two simultaneous-conjugacy (inner Nielsen) classes. The numerical statement N/|G|=2 is correct under the record's explicit convention.
Originality is only for the exact finite census after targeted searches, not a claim that the counting method is new.
